# FPS audit, rrt-019.1, 2026-10-27/28

## Summary

The native client ran at 20 fps (50 ms frames) in a night-time rain scene and
only slightly faster dry or by day, on an RTX 5060. The single confirmed cause
was **client-side wildlife drawing**: `Wildlife._draw` rebuilt every animal
within the 900 m activity radius on every frame, although the view is about
150 m across. That cost about 30 ms per frame and about 2,200 draw calls.
It arrived in `c036e0b` (2026-10-20, after v0.18.0alpha): a 0.19 regression.

Fixed in `ad73953` (only on-screen animals are drawn; they still move and react
off screen): **50.0 -> 19.9 ms per frame (20 -> 50 fps) in night rain, 58 fps dry**.
Then street-light lookups for people (`dc4e955`), one pass for wet roads
(`f7f3b3f`) and one draw call per road layer (`e4cc52d`). Final, night rain,
vsync off: **12.7 ms (78.5 fps), p95 14.4 ms**; rush hour 13.2 ms (75.5 fps),
p95 15.0 ms. With vsync (60 Hz) both hold 60 fps.

The simulation server and the network are not bottlenecks. The remaining ~20 ms
is spread across many client layers; there is no second large single cause.

## Setup

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060, driver 617.42, Windows (WSL2 host) |
| Client | Native Windows Godot 4.7.2, Compatibility renderer (OpenGL 3.3), 1280x720, default zoom |
| Scene | Oulu, taxi parked at Merikosken sillat (427872, 7211248), 36 chunks, 2,502 buildings, 127,153 windows (14,805 lit), 128 animals |
| Weather | `rainserver.py`: rain forced, wetness 1 (or forced dry with `RRT_RAIN=0`) |
| Time | 2026-10-23 22:00 (night) or 12:00 (day), `--no-historical-weather` |
| Measure | `--bench 15..30`: frames after a 5 s warm-up; sections over the same frames |

Reproduce from the repo root (WSL with Windows Godot at `C:\Godot`):

```bash
D=.github/performance-analysis/rrt-019.1-fps-audit-data
$D/bench.sh /abs/out.json 1 --bench 20          # night rain; START=...T12:00 for day; 0 = dry
$D/hide.sh wildlife entities z5                  # one bench per --bench-hide group
python3 $D/show.py /abs/out.json                 # sections per frame
```

Run the benches in the foreground: Windows Godot launched from a background
WSL job exits at once.

## Baseline (before `ad73953`)

| Scene | Frame | FPS | p95 | Draw calls |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Night, rain | 49.7 ms | 20.1 | 55.5 ms | 4,797 |
| Night, dry | 46.9 ms | 21.3 | 52.6 ms | 4,142 |
| Day, dry | 45.6 ms | 21.9 | 51.1 ms | 4,215 |

Night rain frame split (`rain_split.json`):

| Phase | ms/frame |
| --- | ---: |
| All `_process` (main.gd 2.1 of it) | 3.6 |
| Redraws/layout before the render (`_draw` callbacks) | 26.8 |
| Render (viewport CPU 18.6; the GPU timer reports the same number, so it is not a reliable GPU time on this renderer) | 19.3 |

The client is **CPU-bound** on canvas command building and submission, not on
the GPU, vsync (`--disable-vsync`: 49.5 ms) or the render thread mode
(`--render-thread safe`: 50.5 ms).

## Ranked bottlenecks

| # | What | Evidence | Cost | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| 1 | Wildlife drew all 128 animals (flocks of 5, 5-20 commands each) every frame, no view culling | `--bench-hide wildlife`: 50.0 -> 20.4 ms, 4,777 -> 2,597 draw calls; culling: 21.5 ms | ~30 ms | **Fixed**, `ad73953` |
| 2 | `MapLayer.light_at` summed every street light of each nearby chunk, per person (and dog, vehicle, ball) | `--bench-hide entities`: 19.9 -> 16.7 ms; `Perf.time_draws`: `_draw_people` 4.0 ms/frame for 24 people, 3.2 ms of it `light_at` (~130 us a call) | ~3 ms | **Fixed**, `dc4e955`: lights bucketed by 20 m cell; 20.4 -> 17.8 ms, `_draw_people` 1.3 ms |
| 3 | Wet-road layers (z5) in rain | `--bench-hide z5`: 19.9 -> 17.6 ms, -1,000 draw calls; dry 17.1 ms | ~2.5 ms | Confirmed; the whole rain cost |
| 4 | Canvas render of ~2,600 draw calls, 14,000 canvas items, 192,000 primitives | render 10.2-11.2 ms after the fixes; no hidden group removes more than ~2 ms | ~10 ms | Spread over the layers; no single cause |

After the fix, hiding these changed the frame by less than ±1.5 ms (bench
noise): 3D buildings, night beams, light pools, labels, z0-z4, z6-z8, z9-z15,
ground, 2.5D buildings, UI.

## Server and network

`rrt-019-sim-audit-data/bench_sim.py` at the same spot and time (60 s after
30 s warm-up, seed 1; `raw/sim.json`):

- tick wall time: mean 2.3 ms, p50 2.9, p95 3.8, p99 9.8, max 16.1 ms - 30 Hz budget 33 ms, 0 % over budget
- NPC update 1.5 ms of it; state broadcast 0.48 ms; no GC pauses in the measured minute
- state messages: 7.7 KB mean (8.8 KB max), encoded in 0.11 ms; the client parses 1.4 per frame at 0.7 ms each
- the client never waits on the network: the socket is polled without blocking

Entities in this quiet night scene: 2 NPC vehicles, 6 pedestrians, 5 trains,
45 residents. Dense daytime traffic was not part of this measurement; the
earlier `rrt-019-sim-audit-data/raw/oulu_center_17_*` runs cover 17:00 in Oulu
centre (p95 11.4 ms, p99 36 ms).

## Progress (night rain unless noted; RTX 5060, 1280x720)

| After | Frame | FPS | Draw calls | |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| baseline | 49.7 ms | 20.1 | 4,797 | |
| `ad73953` wildlife drawn only on screen | 19.9 ms | 50 | 2,584 | |
| `dc4e955` street light by 20 m cell | 17.8 ms | 56 | 2,638 | |
| `f7f3b3f` wet roads in one pass | 17.1 ms | 58.6 | 2,459 | |
| `e4cc52d` roads in one draw call per layer | 12.7 ms | 78.5 | 1,632 | vsync off (`before_nv`: 16.8 ms at `f7f3b3f`) |
| same, rush hour 17:00 | 13.2 ms | 75.5 | 1,629 | vsync off; 12 NPC vehicles, 64 pedestrians |

Benches from `e4cc52d` on use `GFLAGS=--disable-vsync`: with vsync the
frame sits at exactly 16.7 ms and hides the work.

Bisect detail behind `e4cc52d`: hiding the chunks off screen changed draw
calls by 1 % (Godot already culls them), but hiding z1 (roads) removed 730
and z5 (wet roads, puddles) 895 - each `draw_polyline` was its own draw call.

## Remaining (rush hour, vsync off, `raw/rush_nv.json`)

- render 6.5 ms for ~1,630 draw calls
- scripts and redraws before the render 6.2 ms: main.gd 1.9 ms (present 1.5),
  people 1.4 ms, night beams 0.7 ms, canopy supports 0.5 ms
- the same `Strokes` batching fits other `draw_polyline`-heavy layers
  (railings, fences, paths) if the draw-call count matters again

## Instrumentation (`34aaf3e`, `50c58cd`, `82f7f8c`)

Active only with `--bench`: frame phases, per-chunk-layer redraw times, physics
time, node and canvas counts, `ui`/`wildlife` hide groups, sections reset after
warm-up; each entity-layer redraw timed separately (`Perf.time_draws`);
drawn entity, NPC and pedestrian counts. Overhead without `--bench`: none (a boolean checked once per layer at
creation). With it: two signal callbacks per frame and one closure call per
layer redraw.

## Tests

- `godot/tests/wildlife_render.gd` (with display): passes; fails without the fix
- Godot client suite: 3,489 checks, 0 failed, incl. `test_light_at_cells` and the
  one-pass wet blend check
- `tests/road_strokes.gd` (display): batched strokes vs draw_polyline/multiline,
  max 1/255 on 0.6 % of channels; `tests/wet_road_batching.gd`: 0 changed channels
  (cell lookup equals summing every light, 2,000 random points, one broken light)
- `tests/animal_audio.gd`: passed
- Rendered screenshots inspected: daytime (animals near the view drawn),
  night (street-lit taxi as before), night rain before/after the stroke batching (same)
